policy: Rust suite first: every declaration and source gap requires explicit behavior mapping and passing evidence against the TypeScript gateway before R09+.
inventory_method: TypeScript compiler AST: it/test declarations (including aliases, chained modifiers and parameterized declarations); source fingerprints detect drift.
limits: Declarations inside loops/each are recorded once; runtime expansions and branch coverage require explicit Rust cases.
Static direct imports are triage hints only; unreferenced files are coverage-review gaps, not proof of absent TypeScript tests.
Pending does not claim parity. Merely registering a Rust scenario cannot establish equivalent assertions.
This inventory does not enumerate route/tool/schema/event contracts or prove gateway behavior.

Rust case security.anonymous-routes-denied asserts 401 for exactly those method/path pairs (plus 14 further security routes) with no authorization header, matching the same HTTP surface and status codes. cases.name: does not infer authorization or accept malformed targets
cases.parity_review: The TS declaration asserts 400 for two malformed scope payloads: one omitting every authorization field ({}) and one with authorized:true but a non-literal target (router.local). Rust security.explicit-authorization-required asserts 400 for omitted/false/coerced authorized fields (covering the {} payload), and security.scope-target-validation asserts 400 for router.local and other non-literal-IPv4 targets (covering the second payload). Both Rust cases additionally pin the rejection reason string and prove the rejected scopes leave history unchanged, so the status-code contract the TS test observes is fully covered with stronger error-shape assertions.
